NEONHOME.Title: Neon At Home
NEONHOME.NoCharacter: No character to show. Open the suite from a character you own.

Rules.Name: Carry & Weight Rules
Rules.Label: Edit rules
Rules.Hint: Carry slots by armor class, slot costs, weight limits and default weights, and your own Syndromes.

EnforceCarry.Name: Carry slots
EnforceCarry.Hint: Block: carrying or equipping something past a character's carry slots is stopped with a pop-up, in the Loadout and on the character sheet (the GM can override). Things arriving on a character (bought, looted) aren't refused, only flagged.

EnforceWeight.Name: Weight limit
EnforceWeight.Hint: What happens when a change would put a character over their weight limit.

Enforce.block: Block players (the GM can still do it)

ArmorEffects.Name: Apply armor upgrade bonuses
ArmorEffects.Hint: Keep an effect on each character for the worn armor's upgrades: penalty relief, Plate Padding's Stealth, War Paint's Wardrobe & Style, the AI Armor Interface's Concentration.

DefaultBay.Name: Vehicle bays without a home
DefaultBay.Hint: Bays a character has when Neon Hub doesn't give them a home with parking and you haven't set a number on the character.

PlayerCrafting.Name: Players can make custom attachments
PlayerCrafting.Hint: Lets players create their own attachment items on the Weaponbench. Off: only the GM can.

Syndromes.Name: Syndromes & Inspiration
Syndromes.Hint: The Biomonitor tracks Empathy tiers, Syndromes, Catharsis and Inspiration from the Syndromes & Inspiration homebrew.

CltEncumbered.Name: Condition Lab: Encumbered condition
CltEncumbered.Hint: With Condition Lab & Triggler, a condition of this name is applied when a character goes over the weight limit (its macros, chat and triggers run), with the MOVE penalty added. Without one, Neon At Home's own Encumbered status is used. With Neon Combat Manager running, its Neon Conditions are used instead.

CltOverloaded.Name: Condition Lab: Overloaded condition
CltOverloaded.Hint: The same, for over double the weight limit.

CatharsisAbsorbs.Name: Catharsis takes Humanity Loss first
CatharsisAbsorbs.Hint: When a character with Catharsis loses Humanity, the buffer takes it first and only the rest comes off true Humanity.

Maintenance.Name: Maintenance tab (Breaking Your Stuff)
Maintenance.Hint: Maintenance, inspections, repairs and malfunctions from R. Talsorian's Breaking Your Stuff DLC.

MalfunctionOnFumble.Name: Malfunction on a natural 1
MalfunctionOnFumble.Hint: Roll a malfunction automatically when a check with an item (an attack, a cyberdeck action) rolls a natural 1 and the item is poorly maintained. The GM can always call one from the Maintenance tab.
MalfunctionOnFumble.unmaintained: Damaged gear, or gear a cycle overdue for maintenance

DropHeld.Name: Lost hands drop what they hold
DropHeld.Hint: A Dismembered Arm or Hand (including an EMP'd or Destroyed cyberarm) drops what it was holding: into an Item Piles pile beside the token when Item Piles is on, otherwise it's no longer carried. The GM is asked when it isn't clear which hand held what.

MaintCycleMode.Name: Maintenance months
MaintCycleMode.Hint: Breaking Your Stuff has gear maintained once a month. With Neon Hub, each character's month starts on their calendar's Rent Day, like their Lifestyle bill (or with Neon Hub's month counter, without calendars). Otherwise the GM starts each month, or each week for a faster grind, from the Maintenance tab.
MaintCycleMode.rent: Neon Hub's Rent Day (falls back to monthly without Neon Hub)

DropCyberlimbs.Name: Lost limbs drop their cyberware
DropCyberlimbs.Hint: A Dismembered Arm, Hand or Leg takes the cyberware in it along: a cyberarm or cyberleg with its options, or a hand's cyberhand, cyberfingers and other hand options, dropped where the character stands (an Item Piles pile when it's on). The GM picks the side.

DowntimeStash.Name: Home stash only in downtime
DowntimeStash.Hint: Players reach their home stash (from the Loadout, or for upgrades and attachments) only while they're in downtime. The GM always can.

DowntimeBench.Name: Weaponbench and armor upgrades only in downtime
DowntimeBench.Hint: Attaching and detaching weapon attachments, making custom ones, and fitting or removing armor upgrades happen at home, in downtime. The GM always can.

DowntimeBay.Name: Vehicle Bay changes only in downtime
DowntimeBay.Hint: Parking, swapping, adding and removing vehicles happen in downtime; anyone can look at the bay any time. The GM always can.

DowntimeMaintenance.Name: Maintenance and repairs only in downtime
DowntimeMaintenance.Hint: Maintenance Checks and repairs happen in downtime, and spend the time they take (Breaking Your Stuff; Cyberpunk RED p.140). Inspecting and jury-rigging don't. The GM always can.

DowntimeTab.Name: Downtime tab
DowntimeTab.Hint: Downtime actions from the core rulebook (the Hustle, resting, treatment, repairs, and each Role's work), spending Neon Hub's downtime credits.

SalvageEra.Name: Salvage tables
SalvageEra.Hint: Which Night City salvaging happens in: 2045 (Salvaging Night City's places) or 2070 (one Combat Zone, in Pacifica, and no Hot Zone: the Combat Zone, the scrapyards, the Perimeter and the Badlands, each with its own tables). Automatic follows Neon Hub's lifestyle era.

Perks.Name: Perk Tree
Perks.Hint: The Perk System from Cyberpunk: The Unification Era (Chapter 16): a Perk Tree window for each character, Perk Points, and each perk an effect on the character sheet.

DeckTab.Name: Cyberdeck tab
DeckTab.Hint: The netrunner's quickhack suite (Cyberpunk: The Unification Era, Chapter 10): the deck they run, how it connects, and the Programs, quickhacks and Hardware slotted in it, Program-only and Hardware-only slots kept apart.

State.owned: Owned: not on you (at home, in a car)

Loadout.Title: Loadout
Loadout.CarryOff: The GM has carry slots switched off.
Loadout.NothingOnYou: Nothing on you. Drag things here from your home.
Loadout.NotCarriedHint: On the sheet as owned: not counted against slots or weight. Carry them, or store them at home.

Warn.noArmor: {name} can't be worn with armor: its slots don't count.
Warn.group: {name}: only one of these counts at a time.

Loadout.Stow: Store it (home stash, or the vehicle picked on the right)

Blocked.Title: No room to carry it
Blocked.Body: {item} won't fit: it would put {name} at {used} of {capacity} carry slots.
Blocked.Arrived: {item} has been added, and {name} is now at {used} of {capacity} carry slots. Store something, or set it to owned (not on them).
Blocked.Hint: Store something at home or in a vehicle, mark it as owned (not on you), or wear armor or carry gear with more slots.

Loadout.Overloaded: Overloaded: MOVE 1, and the GM may call for checks
Loadout.OverWeight: Over the weight limit: {current} of {max} units.
Loadout.EffectsOff: The GM has armor upgrade bonuses switched off: apply these at the table.

half.Name: Encumbered
half.Hint: Carrying more than the weight limit: MOVE is halved (rounded down, at least 1). Neon At Home applies and removes it with the load.
half.Card: {name} is carrying more than they can: MOVE is halved until they lighten the load.

one.Name: Overloaded
one.Hint: Carrying more than double the weight limit: MOVE is 1, and the GM may call for checks. Neon At Home applies and removes it with the load.
one.Card: {name} is carrying more than double what they can: MOVE is 1, and the GM may call for checks depending on the situation.

none.Card: {name} is no longer weighed down: MOVE is back to normal.

Upgrade.Title: Armor upgrades
Upgrade.NotWorn: not worn: upgrades do nothing until it is
Upgrade.NoneAvailable: No armor upgrades on you or in your stash.

Reason.location: {name} doesn't fit this part of the armor.
Reason.class: {name} isn't made for this class of armor.

Effect.reliefAll: Removes REF, DEX and MOVE penalties
Effect.warPaint: War Paint (+2 Wardrobe & Style with head and body)
Effect.enviro: Enviro-Shielding (radiation immunity with head and body)
Effect.fireproof: Fireproof padding (can't be set on fire with head and body)

Note.reliefMove: MOVE penalty removed ({value}): apply to MOVE rolls at the table.
Note.fireproof: Fireproof padding: can't be set on fire.
Note.neuroport: Neuro-port: 2 extra neuralware option slots while worn.

Stash.Title: Home storage
Stash.Intro: Your home stash keeps what you aren't carrying. It's a Cyberpunk RED container actor in the Home Stashes folder.
Stash.LinkHint: GM: drop a container actor here to use it as this character's stash instead.
Stash.Name: {name}'s Stash
Stash.Empty: Empty. Drag things here to store them.

Bay.Title: Vehicle Bay
Bay.EmptyBay: Empty bay. Drop a vehicle here.
Bay.NoBays: This home has no vehicle bays. Your vehicles park on the street.
Bay.NoHub: With Neon Hub, bays come from the home's parking. The GM can also set a number here.
Bay.StreetHint: Vehicles without a bay at home.
Bay.StreetEmpty: Nothing on the street. Drop vehicle actors here or into a bay.
Bay.Moved: {n} vehicle(s) lost their bay (the home has fewer bays now).
Bay.NoVas: Install MMuton's CPR Vehicle Actor Sheet for crew seats, mounted weapons and upgrades on vehicle actors.

Bio.Title: Biomonitor
Bio.FlipSide: Move it to the other side
Bio.QuickFirstAid: Quick fix: First Aid DV{a} / Paramedic DV{b}
Bio.AntipathyTip: -2 to Humanity Loss rolls (minimum 1) and -2 to Humanity Gain rolls (minimum 0). Doesn't change Syndromes, except Humanity Loss rolls from a Stressor.
Bio.BreakTip: Extreme cyberpsychosis: every Syndrome plays at its worst. Spend LUCK each round on an Endurance (move) or Concentration (action) save to take back control.
Bio.SystemTip: Registered with MAXTAC: 10% of Housing and Lifestyle in taxes each month; NCPD responds a HEAT rank higher.
Bio.CatharsisHint: Virtual Humanity gained by falling into a deeper Empathy tier. It takes Humanity Loss before true Humanity does.
Bio.TierCard: {name} has fallen into {tier}. Catharsis +{gain}. Pick the tier's Syndromes in the Biomonitor.

Spend.rerollCard: {name} spends an Inspiration on a free reroll.
Spend.luckCard: {name} spends an Inspiration to restore 2 LUCK.
Spend.lootboxCard: {name} spends an Inspiration on a loot box roll.

Bio.Name: Name

Owed.mild: This tier needs a Mild Syndrome ({points}/{need} points).
Owed.severe: This tier needs a Severe Syndrome: upgrade the Mild to Severe or add another Mild, and add a Severe ({points}/{need} points).
Owed.extreme: This tier needs an Extreme Syndrome: upgrade or add a Severe, and add an Extreme ({points}/{need} points).

Bio.NeedsScar: Back at functional Humanity, one {severity} Syndrome stays as a scar. Mark which.
Bio.WorstNote: Complete break: this Syndrome plays at its worst.
Bio.RemoveConfirm: Remove this Syndrome from the character?
Bio.TherapyConfirm: A month of Intensive Therapy (5,000eb): Syndromes lingering at this Humanity are removed, and the scars reset to the current tier. Go ahead?
Bio.TherapyCard: {name} completes a month of Intensive Therapy. The old scars fade.

Cyber.Title: Cyberware
Cyber.NoLink: No Neural Link: neuralware needs one.
Cyber.Hint: Conditions follow Breaking Your Stuff. Damaged cyberware works but can malfunction. Destroyed or EMP'd cyberware is offline with everything installed in it: its bonuses switch off and its weapons can't be rolled. An offline cyberarm or cyberleg counts as a Dismembered Arm or Leg until it works again. Only the GM changes this; see the Maintenance tab to maintain, inspect and repair.
Cyber.GMOnly: Only the GM can change whether gear works.

InjuryNote.emp: {limb} is knocked out by EMP. This goes away by itself when the GM brings it back.
InjuryNote.destroyed: {limb} is Destroyed. This goes away by itself when it's repaired.
InjuryNote.dbr: {limb} is Destroyed Beyond Repair. This goes away when it's uninstalled or replaced.

Bench.Title: Weaponbench
Bench.PickWeapon: Pick a weapon from the rack.
Bench.NoneAttached: Nothing attached. Drag attachments onto the bench.
Bench.DrawerEmpty: No attachments for this weapon on you or in your stash.
Bench.FixedLabel: Fixed: can't be taken off once attached
Bench.BenefitsHint:
Ignores half armor
+2 Stealth while concealed
Bench.Crafted: {name} made. It's on the character, ready to attach.
Bench.NoCrafting: Only the GM can make custom attachments.

Config.SlotsLoose: Slot cost when carried loose (not installed)
Config.ArmorClassHint: Sets carry slots (when worn on the body) and upgrade slots.
Config.CyberwareSlotsHint: While installed, this Subdermal Pocket adds these carry slots. Leave them empty for the default: 2 for gear or a one-handed weapon.
Config.CarryGearHint: When equipped, adds carry slots. "Anything" adds to the general slots; the others are slots only for that.
Config.NoArmor: Can't be used with armor (Light Armorjack or heavier)
Config.KeyHint: A short id. The same key can't be installed twice in one armor, and other upgrades can require it.
Config.Pair: Works only with head and body armor both upgraded
Config.MaintenanceHint: What kind of gear this is decides the skill that maintains it and the value scale (drones and vehicles have their own). The malfunction table is rolled when it malfunctions.

Rules.CarryIntro: From the Armor & Carrying homebrew: the armor worn on the body sets carry slots, and things cost slots by kind. The right column is the spreadsheet's number.
Rules.OwnedCounts: Items marked owned count too (off: owned means not on the character)
Rules.WeightIntro: Weight in units. Items use their own weight (Neon At Home's, or MMuton's Weight System's if set), else these defaults.
Rules.IncludeUpgrades: Attachments add their weight to the item they're on
Rules.Encumbrance: Encumbrance: over the limit MOVE is halved, over double it MOVE is 1
Rules.SyndromesIntro: Your own Syndromes, offered alongside the homebrew's list when a player adds one.

Error.NotFound: That item or actor is gone.
Error.Open: The home window couldn't open. The details are in the console (F12).
Error.Tab: This tab couldn't be shown. The details are in the console (F12).

Card.destroyed: {name}'s {item} is Destroyed: it doesn't work, nor does anything installed in it, until it's repaired.
Card.dbr: {name}'s {item} is Destroyed Beyond Repair. It will never work again.

Card.empOff: {name}'s {item} is back online after the EMP.

Blocked.destroyed: {item} is Destroyed and can't be used until it's repaired.

Maint.Title: Maintenance

NewCycleAsk.month: Start the next month? Gear that isn't covered by Lifestyle needs a new maintenance Check.
NewCycleAsk.week: Start the next week? Gear that isn't covered by Lifestyle needs a new maintenance Check.

NewCycle.month: Month {n} begins. Gear beyond your Lifestyle needs its maintenance Check.
NewCycle.week: Week {n} begins. Gear beyond your Lifestyle needs its maintenance Check.

Maint.CoversUpTo: Covers maintenance of gear worth up to {eb} (drones and vehicles on their own scale).

Tally.covered: Covered by Lifestyle (or looked after by someone else)

Maint.BreakHint: Breaking Your Stuff: gear becomes Damaged at the GM's call. Pick why; the gear that reason usually affects is ticked for you.
Maint.KeepQuiet: Keep it from the players (Damaged gear isn't always obvious)

CauseHint.maintenance: Gear that hasn't been maintained properly.
CauseHint.injury: Gear worn or stowed where the injury landed: a cracked deck, broken smart glasses.
CauseHint.electrocution: A real jolt of electricity damages circuitry (EMP effects don't count here).
CauseHint.environment: Weather or surroundings bad enough to hurt a person hurt their gear too.
CauseHint.excessive: 20 or more damage after SP can damage cyberware, worn gear or a vehicle, even without a Critical Injury.
CauseHint.fire: Two or more Rounds on fire or exposed to radiation.
CauseHint.drugs: Repeated toxins or long-term drug use throw cyberware out of whack.

Maint.HiddenDamage: Damaged, but the players don't know
Maint.HiddenDamageHint: The players see this as working until someone inspects it (DV13) or you reveal it.
Maint.InheritedOffline: Offline because what it's installed in doesn't work.
Maint.WhoWorks: Checks are rolled by {name}. Anyone can maintain anyone's gear; only the owner's Lifestyle covers it.
Maint.CoveredBy: Maintained as part of a {lifestyle} Lifestyle: no Check or time needed.
Maint.CoveredRole: Maintained as part of a {lifestyle} Lifestyle, counted a level higher for a {role}.

Exempt.exec: An Exec's employer maintains gear assigned to their team.
Exempt.medtech: A Medtech's Role Ability gear is looked after for them.
Exempt.nomad: A Nomad's family looks after vehicles and upgrades from their Role Ability.

Maint.DueHint: Worth more than the Lifestyle covers ({lifestyle} or better): it needs a maintenance Check this cycle. A failed Check means starting over.
Maint.WorthDrop: A buyer who knows its condition pays {eb} ({category}); the same in materials for a Tech.
Maint.Worthless: Worthless: practically nobody buys it, and it's no use for crafting.

maintain.fixed: {name} maintains {item} ({time}): it's no longer Damaged, and any malfunction is over.
maintain.fail: {name} realizes halfway through that something went wrong: start over on {item}.

inspect.ok: {name} looks {item} over for a minute: it seems fine.
inspect.fail: {name} can't tell whether anything's wrong with {item}.

rig.ok: {name} jury-rigs {item}: it works properly for {minutes} minutes, then the malfunction returns.

Maint.NoExpertise: {name} needs Field Expertise (a Tech's Maker ability) to jury-rig a malfunction.
Maint.RepairHint: Destroyed gear is repaired to perfect condition with its Tech skill, at a DV and time set by its price (Cyberpunk RED, p.140); a destroyed vehicle is DV17 and a week. On a failure the work starts over.
Maint.RentDay: Rent Day on {calendar}: {month} begins. Gear beyond your Lifestyle needs its maintenance Check.
Maint.HubMonth: {month} begins (Neon Hub). Gear beyond your Lifestyle needs its maintenance Check.
Maint.FollowsRent: Maintenance months start on Neon Hub's Rent Day. Move the calendar on, or change Maintenance months in the module settings.
Maint.ToRentDayAsk: Jump this character's Neon Hub calendar to its next Rent Day? Neon Hub starts the new month for everyone on that calendar (Lifestyle bills, Headquarters), and maintenance falls due.

Reason.gm: The GM calls a malfunction on {name}'s {item}.
Reason.fumble: {name} rolled a natural 1 with a poorly maintained {item}.

Action.dropHeld: Failed: drop what the hand holds

Done.emptyMag: {name}'s {item}: the loaded ammunition is Destroyed Beyond Repair.
Done.missCycle: {item} won't be covered by Lifestyle next cycle.

Reason.severed: (the limb is gone; torn-off cyberware is Destroyed until it's repaired with Cybertech)

Drop.Title: Drop what the hand held
Drop.Ask: {name} lost an arm {side}: drop anything it was holding. Tick what goes.
Drop.PilesSetting: Item Piles can't make piles: its actor type for piles is "{type}". In Item Piles' module settings, open System Specific and reset them to Cyberpunk RED's defaults (or set Actor class type to one of: {types}). Until then, dropped items are just no longer carried.
Drop.PilesQuantity: Item Piles' "Item quantity attribute" is blank, so anything dropped in a pile couldn't be picked up again. In Item Piles' module settings, open System Specific and reset them to Cyberpunk RED's defaults (it's system.amount). Until then, dropped items are just no longer carried.
Drop.LimbAsk: {name} lost {part}. Which side, and what comes off with it?
Drop.Chrome: Cyberware that comes off with it
Drop.CybertechNote: On a cyberlimb: Cybertech can Quick Fix or Treat this instead of First Aid, Paramedic or Surgery, at the same DV and in the same time (Cyberpunk RED, p.223).

Hands.Title: Not enough hands
Hands.One: {name} has one working hand left: the {side} arm or hand is gone.
Hands.None: {name} has no working hands: both arms or hands are gone.
Hands.Hint: Put something down first. A replacement limb, or the cyberarm working again, gives the hand back.

Only.stash: The home stash is reached in downtime.
Only.bench: Workbench jobs (attachments and armor upgrades) are done at home, in downtime.
Only.bay: Parking and swapping vehicles is done in downtime.
Only.maintenance: Maintenance and repairs are done in downtime.
Only.actions: Downtime actions are taken in downtime.

Downtime.NotEnough: {name} needs {need} of downtime and has {left} left.

Badge.tip: The home stash, the workbench, vehicle parking and maintenance wait for downtime (the GM's settings).

Downtime.Title: Downtime
Downtime.Started: {label}: downtime for {names}. Home's open: the stash, the workbench, the garage, maintenance and downtime actions.
Downtime.NotTaking: Not taking part in this downtime
Downtime.HustleOnly: {roles}: the Hustle (Role Abilities that aren't downtime work).
Downtime.DropHere: Drop an item here (from the Items sidebar or a compendium)
Downtime.NeedsRole: Only a {role} can do this; {name} isn't one.
Downtime.NotYourself: Nobody can do a Treatment on themselves, only a Quick Fix (p.222).
Downtime.NeedsMedTech: {name} has no Medical Tech (a Medtech's Medicine).
Downtime.AlreadyUpgraded: {item} already has its Maker upgrade (one per item).
Downtime.DescribeIt: Describe the invention for the GM.
Downtime.NightMarketRank: {name} needs Operator Rank 5 to set up a Night Market.
Downtime.NightMarketMonth: A Night Market has already been set up this month.
Downtime.TimeYours: The corebook doesn't time this; set how long it takes.
Downtime.UpgradeNoted: Noted on the item for the GM to apply.
Downtime.InventNote: Describe it to the GM first; the GM sets its price category (Expensive at the least) and writes its rules.
Downtime.TherapyBoth: A week for the Medtech and for {patient} (from their downtime too, if they're in it).

Blurb.hustle: A week of work on the side between Jobs: roll 1d6 on your Role's table; the pay goes by your Role Ability Rank (Cyberpunk RED, p.381).
Blurb.rest: Each full day of rest heals HP equal to BODY, once stabilized (p.222).
Blurb.treat: A Treatment takes four hours and removes the injury for good, with the skill and DV the injury lists; Cybertech works in their place on a cyberlimb. Nobody can Treat themselves. A few injuries (Torn Muscle, Foreign Object, Concussion) are cured by a Quick Fix, a minute's work you can do on yourself (pp.222-223).
Blurb.workshop: Maintenance Checks and repairs, from the Maintenance tab: each spends its time (Breaking Your Stuff; repairs, p.140).
Blurb.fabricate: Make an item from Tech Materials a price category lower, used when you start. TECH + the skill it's repaired with + Fabrication Expertise against its DV, rolled halfway through its time; a failure there starts it over, the materials unharmed (p.148).
Blurb.upgrade: One upgrade per item, from Tech Materials of its price category (a vehicle's: Very Expensive), used when you start. The check comes halfway; a failure there starts it over, the materials and the item unharmed (p.148).
Blurb.invent: Invent an upgrade or an item. The GM sets its price category, which sets the DV and time; the check comes halfway, and a failure sends you back to the drawing board. A finished invention is a blueprint item the character keeps, and can sell or hand over; Fabrication or Upgrade makes it real (pp.148-149).
Blurb.pharma: An hour and 200eb of materials make as many doses as your Medical Tech Skill, on a DV13 Medical Tech Check; a failure wastes the materials (p.149).
Blurb.therapy: A week for you and your patient, materials bought from Biotechnica, a Medical Tech Check at the end; a failure wastes the week and the materials. You can't treat yourself (p.229).
Blurb.rumor: Hunt a rumor down with an information skill, against the Active DV for how detailed it is (p.151).
Blurb.story: Publish: 1d10 against your Believability, set by Credibility and raised by hard evidence. LUCK can't help (pp.151-153).
Blurb.nightMarket: With Operator Rank 5, once a month, gather other Fixers into a Night Market where anything can be found (p.160).
Blurb.projects: Long work kept going over downtimes: Maker projects and repairs. Put downtime in; the check comes due halfway. Fail it and you realize you have to start over (the materials are fine); pass it and the rest of the time finishes it (Cyberpunk RED pp.140, 148-149).
Blurb.salvage: A week picking through the ruins, and no other downtime that week. Take whatever turns up (1d6 on the place's table) or hunt one category (a harder DV). A Basic Tech Check sets the worth found: pick out Destroyed items of that category (to repair later) or Tech Materials, up to that worth; the rest is lost. A Critical Failure finds nothing and runs into the place's perils (Salvaging Night City).
Blurb.strip: Break gear down into Tech Materials for Maker work: pick items whose worth adds up to the materials you want (Damaged gear is worth a price category less, Destroyed two). Stacks of materials break down or combine the same way. What's past the materials' worth is lost. A few items take no time; a big batch does: past the first 5, each item takes 30 minutes of downtime (materials don't count).
Blurb.perkTraining: A week of intense training aimed at the perk you want (Chapter 16): 2,500eb rolls 2d6, 5,000eb (very intense) rolls 3d6. Each 6 is a Perk Point. Once a month.
Blurb.synth: Street Drug Synthesis (Chapter 08): a recipe, its ingredients, the tools for its complexity, and the time. Each dose is its own roll: INT + Science (Chemistry) + 1d10 against the recipe's DV. Medtechs with a point of Pharmaceuticals add Medical Tech; Techs add Fabrication Expertise. A failure wastes that dose's ingredients.
Blurb.train: Training (Chapter 15): a week with a teacher earns Training Progress toward a Skill's next level, counted like IP. Self-study and Training BDs can run alongside other downtime at the side rate. You can't train past the teacher's maximum, a Skill (×2) needs double, and only a BD, a teacher or a Skill Chip opens a Skill from zero. Push Training once a week: DV15 Endurance (physical) or Concentration for +5.
Blurb.art: Making art (Chapter 13): spend the materials and the time, then roll. A finished piece on an Augmented Reality Art Display (one per piece, no more than the home sleeps) adds Humanity every month.
Blurb.market: Hear of a Night Market this week (Chapter 17): Streetwise DV13 or Trading DV15. Prices are market; anything up to Super Luxury can turn up. Cyberware is installed free on the spot; weapons come with a box of Basic ammo; no refunds.
Blurb.source: Self Sourcing (Chapter 12): a week of calls and meets for one item, within your Role's reach, and you have to know it exists. Fixers, Netrunners (their goods) and Nomads (vehicles) pay market; Medias and Rockerboys pass a Check at the Sourcing DV and pay double.
Blurb.bodysculpt: Bodysculpting (Chapter 08): Standard reshapes a face or a build (no Humanity); Exotic goes further (fur, tails, scales) for 4d6 Humanity Loss. Four hours on the table, a day off their feet after. Nobody sculpts themselves.

Upgrade.simplify: Simplify: future repairs take half the time
Upgrade.exoticSlot: An attachment slot for an Exotic Weapon
Upgrade.exoticAmmo: An Exotic Weapon fires one Non-Basic Ammunition
Upgrade.vehicle: A vehicle upgrade needing Nomad Rank 1

TherapyEffect.addiction: Frees the patient of one addiction (they fail its Secondary Effect rolls for a year after).
TherapyEffect.standard: Restores 2d6 Humanity (never past the maximum their cyberware leaves).
TherapyEffect.extreme: Restores 4d6 Humanity (never past the maximum their cyberware leaves).

Downtime.RestCard: {name} rested for {days} day(s) and healed {hp} HP.

Fabricate.fail: Halfway through, {name} has to start {item} over. The materials are fine.

UpgradeResult.noted: {name} upgrades {item} ({eb} of materials); the GM applies what it does.
UpgradeResult.fail: Halfway through, {name} has to start the upgrade to {item} over. The materials and the item are fine.

Invent.ok: {name} works it out ({category}): the GM writes up how it works. Fabrication or Upgrade makes it real.
Invent.fail: {name} has to go back to the drawing board.

Pharma.fail: {name}'s batch of {drug} is ruined; the materials are wasted.

TherapyResult.ok: {name}'s week of therapy works: {patient} regains {n} Humanity.
TherapyResult.addiction: {name}'s week of therapy works: {patient} is free of an addiction (the GM notes which).
TherapyResult.fail: {name}'s week with {patient} was for nothing; the materials are lost.

RumorResult.ok: {name} runs down a {depth}: the GM says what it is.

StoryResult.ok: {name} publishes: rolled {roll} on a {chance} in 10. The audience buys it.
StoryResult.fail: {name} publishes: rolled {roll} on a {chance} in 10. The audience doesn't buy it.

Downtime.NightMarketCard: {name} sets up a Night Market with other Fixers: anything can be found there, for a little while.
Downtime.NotIn: {name} isn't taking part in this downtime: downtime actions spend their own downtime.
Downtime.MakesBlueprint: A blueprint of it, kept by the inventor (sellable and transferable)
Downtime.InventValueHint: The figure the GM gives for the idea; it sets the price category. Leave it empty to go by the category. Super Luxury takes a month per 10,000eb.
Downtime.InventTooCheap: An invention is Expensive (500eb) at the least.
Downtime.TrainingCard: {name} trains for a week{aim}: rolled {dice}, {n} six(es): {n} Perk Point(s).
Downtime.TrainingMonth: {name} has already trained for perks this month.

InterestingText.contact: someone from the job remembers you kindly; the GM makes them an NPC you can call on.
InterestingText.opportunity: a lead on paying work: a gig for the crew, an HQ Gig, or a seat at a Night Market.
InterestingText.insideInfo: a rumor worth money: a shipment's route, a rival's weak spot, a door code. The GM decides how true it is.
InterestingText.strings: a contact or an opportunity, with a favor owed or a curious faction: +1 Standing with someone, −1 with their rival.

Downtime.InterestingNote: A d100 too: an Interesting Hustle at {z} or under on a dry week (Z), {l} low (L), {m} good (M), {h} great (H). 01 is a Jackpot.

Project.HowItGoes: Kept on your projects: put downtime in now or later; the check comes halfway.
Project.NoTime: No downtime left to put in.
Project.None: No projects under way. Start one from Fabricate, Upgrade, Invent, or a repair.
Project.AbandonAsk: Give up on this project? The time and materials already spent stay spent.

Check.ok: Halfway through {label}, it's going right for {name}: {left} more finishes it.
Check.fail: Halfway through {label}, {name} realizes it has to start over ({lost} lost; the materials are fine).

Done.upgradeNoted: {name} finishes upgrading {item}; the GM applies what it does.
Done.invent: {name} has a working design ({category}): {blueprint}. The GM writes up how it works; Fabrication or Upgrade makes it real.

Project.Pick: How much downtime to put in
Project.TooMuch: More than there is: {max} at most.
Project.PickSome: Pick how much downtime to put in now.
Project.StartIsNew: Starting here begins a new project.

Materials.Short: {name} needs {materials}: strip gear for parts, salvage some, or source it.

Salvage.Label: Salvage: {place}
Salvage.Roll: TECH + Basic Tech + 1d10: the total sets the worth
Salvage.FumbleNote: Nothing found, and a roll on the place's Perils of Salvaging.

2045.hotZone: What the 2023 bomb left of the old Corp Plaza in the middle of the city: rubble, and radiation.
2045.combatZone: South Night City, the Old Combat Zone, Old Japantown or Little China: picked over for years, and every block is somebody's turf.
2045.scrapyards: Junk waiting on recycling that's always behind, owned by Corps whose security shoots first.
2045.perimeter: Ghost towns, service stations, motels and factories at the city's edge and out in the Badlands. Nomads, who let you be if you don't want what they want.

2070.combatZone: Night City's only Combat Zone: Pacifica's dead resort district, the Voodoo Boys' turf and BARGHEST's Dogtown, worked by gangs and scavs alike.
2070.scrapyards: Coronado Dam's dump in Santo Domingo and Northside's gutted factories: Corp security, NCPD sweeps, and Maelstrom next door.
2070.perimeter: Where the city gives out: abandoned motels, service stations and Unification War leftovers. Raiders, and Nomads.
2070.badlands: Climate-wrecked desert past the Perimeter: wrecks, old war sites, Nomad clans, and raiders like the Wraiths.

Salvage.CritFail: {name} rolls a Critical Failure: nothing salvaged, and trouble.
Salvage.Nothing: {name} spends the week in {place} and finds nothing worth hauling home.
Salvage.Found: {name} hauls {eb} of {category} out of {place}. Pick it out in Downtime, Salvage: Destroyed items of that category, or Tech Materials.
Salvage.FoundRolled: {name} hauls {eb} of {category} (rolled {roll}) out of {place}. Pick it out in Downtime, Salvage: Destroyed items of that category, or Tech Materials.
Salvage.Damage: {n} damage ({dice}); armor soaks it as usual.
Salvage.Rounds: {rounds} rounds in it: {n} damage straight to HP.
Salvage.Resist: Beat DV{dv} {skill}, or take {dice} straight to HP.
Salvage.Injury: {name} also takes {injury} (Critical Injury to the Body).
Salvage.RollInjury: Roll a Critical Injury to the Body from the character sheet.
Salvage.Source: Salvaging Night City p.5, summarized; Cyberpunk RED pp.180-181, 221, 355
Salvage.TooDear: That's more than the {left} left in the haul.
Salvage.DropFind: Drop an item from the Items sidebar or a compendium.
Salvage.Taken: {name} picks {item} out of the haul ({left} left).
Salvage.TakenLast: {name} picks {item} out of the haul: that's all of it.
Salvage.Left: {name} leaves the rest of the haul behind ({left} lost).
Salvage.DropHere: Drop a find here ({category}): it comes Destroyed, to repair later
Salvage.LeaveAsk: Leave what's left of this haul behind? Unspent worth is lost.
Salvage.CrewHint: Each rolls their own week; the crew shares one Perils roll and one Who Turns Up.
Salvage.NotYours: You can't roll {name}'s week: their player (or the GM) has to.

Who.trouble: Trouble that can be talked down: talk, sneak or fight.

Strip.Nothing: {name} has no gear to strip (it can't be equipped, installed, or holding anything installed).
Strip.CardWaste: {name} strips {items} for parts: {materials} ({waste} of it too small to use).
Strip.TimeBatch: {time}: {n} items, the first {free} free, then {each} each
Strip.Label: Strip for parts: {materials}

Blueprint.Name: Blueprint: {name}
Blueprint.Note: A Tech's working design. Fabrication or Upgrade Expertise makes it real; the GM has the final say on its rules. It can be sold or handed over like any gear.
Blueprint.DropHere: Drop the item this blueprint makes (from the Items sidebar, a compendium or a sheet)
Blueprint.MakesHint: Write the invention up as a real item (its type, stats and rules), then drop it here: Fabricating from this blueprint makes a copy of it. A copy is kept on the blueprint, so it goes wherever the blueprint goes. With nothing here, Fabrication makes a plain gear item from the design.
Blueprint.Unlink: Unlink: Fabrication makes a plain gear item again
Blueprint.NotABlueprint: A blueprint can't make a blueprint.
Blueprint.NotHeld: {name} needs {blueprint} on hand to build from it.
Blueprint.Linked: {blueprint}: makes the GM's write-up of it
Blueprint.Plain: {blueprint}: no item linked yet, so a plain gear item from the design (the GM can link one in the blueprint's Home settings)

Perks.Title: Perk Tree
Perks.PointsTip: Available out of all earned: 3 to start, 1 per Role rank raised with IP (not Ganger or Exec), and what the GM awards (big moments, training).
Perks.KillsHint: Kept by you; the GM counts too
Perks.RebaseTip: Count Role ranks raised from now on: the ranks the character has now become their starting ranks.
Perks.NoneYet: No perks yet. Pick one in the tree and unlock it.
Perks.DeedTip: Something done in play: the GM confirms it
Perks.Confirmed: The GM confirmed what this takes in play.
Perks.AwaitGM: What this takes in play waits for the GM to confirm it.
Perks.FxNote: An effect on the sheet with this perk's text, switched on and off with the sheet's own toggle; the GM applies what it does.
Perks.FxToggle: Its effect on the sheet switches on and off with the sheet's own toggle (or here). Situational ones are offered in the roll dialog.
Perks.SlotNote: One {slot} at a time. Drop it for 1 Perk Point to free the slot.
Perks.RefundNote: Its text says when it's refunded: the GM refunds it then.
Perks.ForceTip: GM: unlock it for its points without the requirements.
Perks.FreeTip: GM: unlock it without its requirements or points.
Perks.PickStat: Which STAT does it raise? (max {cap}; no perk raises a STAT above 10)
Perks.ChooseNote: +1 to a STAT you pick when you unlock it

Fiend.heads: {name}'s Perk Fiend coin comes up heads: +1 Perk Point.
Fiend.tails: {name}'s Perk Fiend coin comes up tails: {n} Humanity Loss.

Card.refund: {name}'s perk {perk} is refunded ({cost} Perk Point(s) back).
Card.gone: {name}'s perk {perk} is refunded and gone for good.
Card.lose: {name} loses the perk {perk}, and its points with it.
Card.drop: {name} drops {perk} for 1 Perk Point, freeing the slot.

Ask.refund: Refund this perk? Its points come back, and it can be bought again.
Ask.gone: Refund this perk for good? Its points come back, and it can't be bought again.
Ask.lose: Take this perk away with its points (lost, not refunded)?
Ask.drop: Drop this specialty for 1 Perk Point? Its own points stay spent; the slot is free for another.

Block.slot: {name} already holds a specialty of that kind: drop it first (1 Perk Point).
Block.dormant: {perk} is switched off until its requirements are met again.

Kind.art: Art Skill (Paint/Draw/Sculpt, Photography/Film, Forgery, Acting, Play Instrument)
Kind.control: Control Skill (Drive, Pilot Air or Pilot Sea)

Deck.Title: Cyberdeck

LinkHint.suite: 20m to architectures, 50m to Neuroports and vehicles. Its deck changes at a clinic (1 hour).
LinkHint.hand: 6m (8m with a Range Upgrade). Plugged in to the Personal Link or Interface Plugs.
LinkHint.arm: Built into the cyberarm: +1 slot (more with Integrated Cyberdeck Upgrades).

Deck.RangeHint: to Neuroports and vehicles; {arch}m to architectures
Deck.InCombat: In combat: Programs and Hardware swap out of combat (a minute each). Switching decks is a Meat Action.
Deck.Over: More than the deck holds as it's connected now:
Deck.UnslotStash: Take it out, to the stash
Deck.BuiltIn: Built into the {suite} (no slots, can't be removed)
Deck.PickDeck: Pick the deck this character runs, above.
Deck.GetDeck: No cyberdeck on this character. Drop one onto their sheet (the Netrunning Gear (2070) compendium has the 2070 decks).
Deck.WontFit: No room for it in the deck's slots of its kind
Deck.EmptyTab: Nothing of this kind on the character.
Deck.Compendium: Quickhacks, quickhack hardware, the 2070 decks and Cybersuites are in the Netrunning Gear (2070) compendium; Deep Dive programs and core hardware in Cyberpunk RED's.
Deck.NotInCombat: Programs and Hardware are swapped out of combat (a minute each).
Deck.Clinic: Putting a deck in or out of a Cybersuite is a Clinic job (an hour): {name} needs downtime for it, or the GM.
Deck.NoRoom: No room for {item}: the deck's {kind} slots are full.
Deck.SuiteHow: Cybersuites are neuralware (Hospital, HL 7, one Neural Link slot): installed or swapped like any cyberware, from the character sheet, with its Humanity Loss. One holds the deck at a time.

Dive.Title: Deep Dive
Dive.PickArch: Pick an architecture on the left, or roll a new one.
Dive.GenerateHint: By the book's steps: 3d6 floors, a d10 for each branch, the Lobby on 1d6 and the rest on the difficulty's 3d6 table. It's saved as a Cyberpunk RED NET Architecture item.
Dive.ArchNote: A {difficulty} NET Architecture (DV{dv}), rolled with Neon At Home.
Dive.IceHint: Black ICE by id, comma separated: {list}
Dive.NeedDeck: Equip a cyberdeck to dive (the Cyberdeck tab).
Dive.QuietIn: Quietly (one more NET Action: Cloak against the Demon watching)
Dive.JackInHint: Jacking in takes a NET Action, and you get +1 NET Action a Turn while under. The rig sets how long you're safe: an Ice Bath 1 hour, a Netrunning Chair 8 hours, an Immersion Cradle indefinitely (and +1 to every Interface Check). Past that, Burnout: 1d6 brain damage at the start of each Turn.
Dive.NoPrograms: No Programs installed in the deck.

Ask.safe: Jack out safely? It takes a NET Action, and the architecture resets behind you.
Ask.unsafe: Eject them? Every Rezzed Black ICE they've met gets one last hit on the way out.

Quiet.seen: {name} tries to slip in to {arch} quietly ({me} vs {them}), and the Demon sees them.

Dive.NoArch: That NET Architecture is gone, or has no floors.
Dive.NotAdjacent: You can only move one floor at a time: down, or back up.
Dive.Locked: A Kraken holds you: you can't move or Jack Out this Turn.
Dive.NoActions: No NET Actions left this Turn.
Dive.OncePerRound: {program} can only be Rezzed or Derezzed once a Turn.

Need.node: There's no Control Node to take here.
Need.controlled: Take Control of the Node first.
Need.slide: There's no Black ICE to Slide away from (or you've Slid this Turn).
Need.bottom: A Virus goes in on the architecture's bottom floor.
Need.target: Pick a target that's still Rezzed.

Meet.won: {name} is faster than {ice} ({me} vs {them}): they act first.
Meet.lost: {ice} is faster than {name} ({them} vs {me}): it acts first.

slide.ok: {name} Slides away from the Black ICE ({them} to beat).
slide.fail: {name} can't shake the Black ICE ({them} to beat).

Result.cloak: {name} Cloaks their tracks: {n} to beat for anyone looking for them.

Effect.locked: It holds them: no going deeper or safe Jack Out until their next Turn ends.
Effect.slowed: One less NET Action next Turn.
Effect.fire: Their deck and clothes are On Fire: 2 damage each Turn until it's put out.
Effect.skunk: −2 to Slide while it's Rezzed (it stacks).
Effect.brainArmor: {n} damage to the brain (Armor took 4 of {rolled}).

Demon.searchMissed: {demon} looks for {name} and misses them ({them} vs {me}).

Dive.Burnout: {name} is past the rig's safe time: Burnout.

Medtech.NeedPoints: {name} needs 4 points in a Medtech Specialty to do Maker work with it.
Medtech.NeedRipperdoc: {name} needs 4 points in Ripperdoc (Surgery) to blueprint cyberware.
Medtech.OnlyCyberware: A Ripperdoc's Maker work is implantable cyberware only.
Medtech.OnlyCryo: Cryosystem Maker work is Cryotank and Cryopump gear only.
Medtech.NeedBlueprint: A Ripperdoc fabricates from a blueprint: source a real piece and blueprint it first.
Medtech.NeedPiece: Pick a real piece of cyberware the character has.
Medtech.Blueprinted: {name} takes a real {item} apart on paper: a blueprint to fabricate it from.
Medtech.RipperdocFab: Ripperdoc: implantable cyberware, from a blueprint of a real piece (drop the piece to blueprint it).
Medtech.CryoFab: Cryosystem: Cryotank and Cryopump mods and upgrades only.
Medtech.RipperdocInvent: Ripperdoc: new implantable cyberware. The GM writes it up and sets its Price Category.
Medtech.CryoInvent: Cryosystem: new Cryotank and Cryopump mods and upgrades. The GM writes it up and sets its Price Category.

Drug.RecipeNote: Teach it to anyone in an hour. Cook it with Street Drug Synthesis (Downtime).
Drug.DoseCostHint: The GM's call. The Item Compendium's drugs run 10–1,500eb a dose.
Drug.DosesHint: A roll, the time and the ingredients for each.
Drug.InventNote: Pharmaceuticals (4+): invent a new street drug or pharmaceutical. The GM writes up what it does and sets its Price Category; the recipe's complexity sets how hard it is to cook.
Drug.MakesRecipe: A recipe item for the drug, to cook with Street Drug Synthesis, teach or sell.
Drug.Invented: {name} works out a new drug: {recipe} ({tier} recipe).
Drug.WhereRecipes: Recipes come from Night Markets and gang or corp stores (the Drug Lab compendium has the book's), or a Pharmaceuticals Medtech invents them.
Drug.NeedTool: {name} needs a {tool} (or better) for this recipe.
Drug.CostHalved: {each} a dose, halved by the Fabrication Station ({total})
Drug.FailNote: A failure wastes that dose's ingredients.

Cook.fail: {name} ruins a batch of {drug} ({n} of {of}): the ingredients are wasted.

Drug.BookDrug: A book street drug (Fabrication Station halves it)
Drug.MakesHint: Cooking it makes this drug. Without one, the drug of that name from Cyberpunk RED's compendium, else a plain drug item.

Train.SideNote: On the side: it runs alongside your other downtime and takes no week of its own.
Train.BdNote: You need that Skill's Training BD in hand (500eb, or 1,000eb for a Skill ×2).
Train.PushNote: Success +5; failure half (round down); an implode nothing (a physical Skill also costs 2d6 damage; anything else leaves you fatigued, −2, all next week).

Why.zero: Self-study can't open {skill} from zero: a Training BD, a teacher or a Skill Chip can.
Why.double: {skill} is a Skill (×2): it can't be self-studied (a Skill Chip lets you).
Why.max: This teacher only takes you to {max}.
Why.academic: Night City University teaches Education, Technique and Performance Skills, not {skill}.

Train.NotYourself: You can't be your own crewmate teacher.
Train.NoCrewmate: No crewmate has {skill} at 6 or more.
Train.NotEnrolled: Enroll at NCU first: DV13 Bureaucracy, or a 1,500eb donation (and a Generic PrePak lifestyle or better).

Enrolled.ok: {name} is enrolled at Night City University.
Enrolled.donated: {name} makes a donation and is enrolled at Night City University.

Train.Label: Training {skill}
Train.LevelUp: {name} trains {skill} ({teacher}): +{n} progress, and {skill} goes up to {level}. {have} carried toward the next.

Push.implode: Pushed too far: nothing this week.

Source.KnowIt: You have to know it exists: a screamsheet, a newsletter, something overheard or seen in play.

Goods.netrunner: Netrunners source quickhacks, deck gear and NET Architectures.
Goods.nomad: Nomads source vehicles and vehicle upgrades their Moto Rank unlocks.

Source.NoRole: {name} can't source: Fixers, Medias, Rockerboys, Netrunners and Nomads can.
Source.OffTheShelf: {item} is off the shelf (Premium or less): just buy it.
Source.Label: Sourcing {item}
Source.fail: {name} spends the week chasing {item}, and comes up empty.
Source.Haggle: A Fixer can Haggle for their Rank's discount (a critical failure means a markup).

Art.Note: Music and acting take two skills (compose, then perform): the performance roll sets the quality. Roll the one that does.
Art.Label: Making {title}
Art.About: {quality} art by {name} ({skill}). On an Augmented Reality Art Display: +{n} Humanity every month.
Art.fail: {name} can't make {title} work: the materials are gone.

Sculpt.Note: A failure wastes the materials and 2 hours; the patient is fine and can try again. Anyone who knew them needs DV17 Human Perception to recognize the new face (DV13 if they knew them well).
Sculpt.fail: {name} can't get {patient}'s new look right: the materials are wasted.

Market.Rules: Market prices (a Fixer can Haggle). Every quality of an item that turns up is for sale. Cyberware installed free on the spot; weapons come with a box of Basic ammo; no refunds.
Market.Note: Found: two categories on sale, 1d10 items each from the On the Shelves table.
Market.found: {name} hears where tonight's Night Market is.
Market.missed: {name} asks around all day and hears nothing.

Place.cryoMedtech: A Medtech's licensed cryotank (500eb a night)

Rest.Double: Double healing: 2 × BODY a day (a cryotank, or Enhanced Antibodies).

Plan.NoCall: {name} has no plan that comes when called.
Plan.ReoFirst: REO Meatsavers' wagon beats them there in {n}, looking for business.
Plan.Label: Health plan
